title: Prefetch-driven admission controller with heterogeneous kernel switcher
creator: Liam Chen
description: Improve continuous batching robustness and tail latency by combining lightweight KV prefetch probes, request-level admission decisions based on short-term sequence-length forecasts, and a heterogeneous-kernel switcher that selects optimized kernels at admission time. The goal is to reduce p99 tail spikes during mixed-sequence workloads while keeping avg token cost neutral or improved.
background: We see recurrent p99 spikes when small/short-prefill requests interleave with long-prefill ones and when kernel choices (fp16 vs int8 vs attention-optimized kernels) are made too late in the pipeline. Existing admission logic is purely queue-length based and kernel selection happens at decode time, causing wasted scheduling and cold kernel penalties. This ticket experiments with prefetch-driven admission: run a lightweight KV/attention probe and sequence-length estimator immediately after request arrival to decide admit/delay and to pick the kernel variant for the prefill+decode path.
proposal: 1) Add a 1-2ms 'prefetch probe' executed in the ingress path that fetches minimal KV metadata and runs a tiny attention-cost estimator. 2) Use a short rolling window forecast (exponential decay over last 2s) of sequence-length distribution to compute a per-request admission score combining deadline slack and kernel warm/cold cost. 3) Attach a kernel_hint to the request (e.g., attention-fast, cost-min, quantized-safe) chosen by a policy that balances latency SLOs and GPU utilization. 4) Admission controller can: accept immediately, defer by X ms to coalesce, or bump to a slow-path queue with reserved slots and prefetched KVs. 5) Implement a 'kernel switcher' that binds the kernel_hint to a pre-reserved kernel context to avoid late kernel swaps during decode.
implementation_notes:
- Prefetch probe runs on CPU+small GPU kernel probe (tiny attention pass using 1-2 tokens) and must be asynchronous but ordered before admission decision.
- Kernel hints map to runtime kernel families; add mapping table in kernel registry.
- Admission decisions update token deadlines and emit events for observability.
- Need careful accounting to avoid probe thrash under bursty traffic: throttle probes per tenant and fallback to conservative admission when probe budget exhausted.
- Add metrics: probe_latency, probe_failure_rate, kernel_hint_match_rate, admission_deferrals, admitted_via_defer, admitted_via_reserved_slot.
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces late kernel swaps, allows smarter coalescing, reduces p99 by preventing mismatched long jobs from disrupting small jobs. Cons: probes add overhead (CPU/GPU cycles), increased complexity in admission logic, potential to mis-predict sequence lengths and mis-route requests. We'll cap probe rate and include fallback heuristics.
metrics: Primary: p95/p99 prefill latency, decode p95/p99, token throughput, cost per 1k tokens. Secondary: probe_latency (ms), kernel_hint_match_rate (%), deferred_admit_ratio (%), SLA error rate. Success criteria: p99 prefill latency reduced by >=20% on mixed workloads and no more than 5% regression in avg token cost.
risks:
- Probe overload during high-QPS could add CPU pressure; mitigate via per-tenant probe budgets.
- Incorrect kernel_hint mapping could increase runtime cost; ensure canary and rollback.
- Complexity increases risk of bugs in rollback scenarios; implement clear circuit-breaker to disable admission probe for a tenant or pool.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for kernel_hint mapper and admission scoring. 2) Integration test in redwood-staging with synthetic traffic generator (mix of 4 token, 64 token, 1024 token distributions) measuring p50/p95/p99. 3) Load test on a two-node dedicated pool mimicking customer X's workload. 4) Small canary on dedicated pool: 1% traffic for 48h, compare metrics to control. 5) Manual chaos: kill kernel contexts to validate fallback to slow-path queue.
rollout_plan:
- Feature flag gated (runtime.prefetch_admission).
- Step 1: enable probe-only (no admission change) to collect telemetry for 1 week.
- Step 2: enable admission with conservative thresholds on staging.
- Step 3: canary on dedicated pool (1%-5% traffic) and run 48-72h.
- Step 4: ramp to 25% then 100% with monitoring and automated rollback if p99 regresses >10%.
